Half the munitions used in the last war originated on this world.|[[Warren Sedoru]]|}} '''Balmorra''' was a [[Factory world/Legends|factory world]] that was located within the [[Balmorra system/Legends|Balmorra system]], situated in a strategic position between the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] and the border of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. Due to its intense industrial manufacturing, it was known as one of the most important foundry worlds in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic's]] space, where some of the most advanced weaponry and [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] were constantly produced throughout most of the planet's history. ==Description== Since Balmorra was very rich in [[Iron/Legends|iron]] and other minerals, it gradually became one of the most recognizable factory worlds in [[the galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Large parts of Balmorra's surface were covered in industrial wastelands, which still contained most of the earliest assembly lines and refineries on the planet. Although manufacturing weaponary was the primary source of profit for the Balmorran economy, the planet's atmosphere suffered greatly from the high levels of pollution which were emitted from the countless industrial plants. Wide plains and urban areas were also located on Balmorra's surface, like the planet's capital [[Bin Prime]]. The [[Balmorran metal parasite]]s which feasted on metals in these urban areas were a long-term problem for the Balmorran government. The [[Balmorra flu]] was also presumably from the world. ==History== The [[Planet/Legends|world]] began as a colony of [[Humbarine/Legends|Humbarine]]. Due to slow interstellar travel and communications, it was one of several colony worlds that declared their independence. During the settlement of Balmorra, while the Republic was still in its infancy, Balmorra quickly established itself as a haven for renowned weapon and battle droid manufacturers. While determined to remain independent of the Republic, they became strong allies supplying the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the greater galaxy with advanced droids and weapons.{{HolonetOld|planets|balmorra|Balmorra}} ===Republic era=== {{Quote|Technically, Balmorra's not a Republic world, just a Republic ''ally.'' But the Empire didn't care.|[[Tai Cordan]]|}} [[File:Markaran_Wastes.png|left|thumb|220x220px|The landscape of [[Markaran Wastes]] on Balmorra.]] Balmorra joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] prior to the [[Indecta Era]]. During the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]], it supported [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Balmorra was the site of a [[Battle of Balmorra (Hundred-Year Darkness)|battle]] during the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]]. In that conflict, [[Leviathan (creature)|Leviathans]] bred by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] splintered the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] barricades on the planet.''[[Star Wars: Book of Sith]]'' During the [[Great Galactic War]] the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] resolved to seize Balmorra due to their military manufacturing plants and strategic location close to the Core Worlds. The Republic immediately sent soldiers to prevent that from happening. As the Great Galactic War continued and the Sith Empire's control continued to spread, the strained Republic began removing forces from Balmorra for redeployment to more important conflicts. This continued until the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] was signed. The Republic base designated [[Base 11A|11A]] had been established on Balmorra and was still under Republic control until the Treaty was signed. The commander of the base, General [[Buryn]] was assigned to leave the base with his troops as per the terms of the Treaty. General Buryn wanted to fulfill his orders, but the Jedi [[Fortris Gall]] insisted that the Republic team that was held captive by the Sith, [[Demolitions Squad 419]], had to be freed first. The Jedi travelled to the [[Troida Military Workshop]], where the soldiers were held hostage, without Buryn's permission.''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 2: New Galactic Order]]'' Issue 1 Buryn chose to remain on-planet after the Treaty's enforced deadline and waited for Fortis. Master [[Orgus Din]] soon joined the General and Jedi Fortis, to convince them both to leave the planet in an attempt to prevent further battles with the Sith, and to begin following the terms of the Treaty.''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 2: New Galactic Order]]'' Issue 6 [[File:Camp_Traken-4.png|thumb|200px|A military base on Balmorra during the Cold War]] Following the treaty and the beginning of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], the Republic was forced to officially end its support for Balmorra. However, a small underground Republic force was left on the planet to aid in a resistance against the remaining Sith Empire. Despite this, most [[Balmorran]]s shared the view that they had been abandoned by the Republic. Surprisingly, the remaining underground resistance prevented the Sith Empire from ever taking complete control of the planet. A number of years after the treaty was signed, with the fragile brokered peace between the Sith Empire remaining, the Republic began reintroducing Republic forces to the planet. While the Balmorrans were receptive to the assistance, their resentment of being abandoned in the past remained. At the same time, the Sith Empire attempted to escalate their presence on the planet in a further bid to claim Balmorra's battle droids and weaponry. Sometime during the [[Eternal Empire]]'s invasion of the galaxy, [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Arcann]] and [[Thexan]] of the Eternal Empire led an assault on Balmorra. The [[Eternal Flagship]] swiftly knocked out Balmorra's planetary defense system, allowing the twin princes to capture the world's weapon factories intact. The Eternal Empire then placed a [[Star Fortress]] around the planet in command of the Exarch [[Malforia]]. Malforia was then kidnapped by the spymaster known as the [[Shroud (disambiguation)|Shroud]], who later had the Star Fortress destroyed, leaving the planet temporarily free from Eternal Empire oppression. At one point, the planet was the headquarters of [[Rigorra]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]].''[[Star Wars Adventures 6: The Warlords of Balmorra]]'' Prior to the Clone Wars, Balmorran corporations were part of the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]], which produced [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droid]]s on the planet. The planet initially refused to secede when the war erupted. However, when the Republic tried to close the Techno Union droid factories, Balmorra eventually joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. The planet seceded from the Galactic Republic in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] and was given a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleships]] to defend it. Balmorra was also the headquarters of [[Balmorran Arms/Legends|Balmorran Arms]], which manufactured [[SD-6 Hulk infantry droid]]s. ===Imperial era=== {{Quote|Okay, Beltane—you've ''proved'' your point. What do you ''want'' for those new droids?"
"You can have them ''cheaply'', Sedriss—Balmorra wants ''freedom'', no more, no less. Once we are free, we'll ''sell'' you arms on a contract basis…if we ''choose'' to.|Executor Sedriss QL and Governor Beltane, following the Battle of Balmorra|}} [[File:Balmorra_surface_view.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Balmorra's surface with [[Bin Prime]] seen from orbit, ca. [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]].]] Under the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Hinch Beltane]] ran the planet and oversaw production there. During the reign of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], the Balmorrans manufactured weapons for the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]], maintained strong ties to [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], and were the primary builders of the [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|AT-ST walker]], [[All Terrain Armored Transport]], and the bulk of the Empire's other armored and ground vehicles. The Balmorrans longed for independence from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], wishing for a free market on which to sell their vaunted weapons technologies. Although there was mutual good feeling between the Rebel Alliance and the natives of Balmorra, liberation would have been impossible, as the planet was well-defended and isolated from the other planets held by the Rebels. Instead, the Alliance launched a hit-and-run [[Raid on Balmorra|sabotage effort]], using the cover of the night to go undetected by Imperial [[Sensor array/Legends|sensor arrays]]. It was not until [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] had demolished much of the weaponry under construction in the [[Imperial construction yard|yards]] that any kind of serious retaliation force was launched. By [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the planet had become an Imperial [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress world]]. Balmorra remained under Imperial control until at least [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]]. [[Standard year/Legends|Years]] later, the planet was liberated by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], and it remained independent for years. Balmorra was brought back into Imperial service during the Emperor's reappearance, but following Palpatine's supposed death near [[Da Soocha]], the rebellious Balmorrans began arming the New Republic. [[File:Battle_of_Balmorra.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Balmorra's capital is attacked by forces under [[Maximilian Veers/Legends|Maximilian Veers]].]] In retaliation, the planet was [[Battle of Balmorra|attacked]] by a force under the command of Military Executor [[Sedriss QL]], including [[Shadow Droid]]s and [[SD-9 battle droid|SD-9-series battle droids]]. After suffering surprising losses at the hands of Balmorra's [[SD-10 battle droid]]s and new [[X-1 Viper|Viper Automatons]], Sedriss called off his attack in exchange for a shipment of the molecularly-shielded droids. ===Later history=== During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] for Balmorra offered any planet ground-based [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] and planetary shield generators in exchange for protection by a fleet during a panicked session of the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|Senate]].''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]'' During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], elements of the [[Confederation Fleet]] attacked Balmorra in their push to reach the Core Worlds. This resulted in the [[Second Battle of Balmorra]]. ==Behind the scenes== The PC video game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] mistakenly places Balmorra in the Sesswenna [[Sector/Legends|sector]] (a misspelling of the true [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]]) of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Galactic Core]]. The Seswenna sector is [[canon]]ically located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].
